paragraphs.text: Dear sisters and elders, I hope your day is being made great through your choices and actions. No new updates to share with you, but continued and increasing optimism on my side for sure. Hopefully on yours as well.

Today I want to share a great story with you that will hopefully inspire you to see the power of each day when used wisely. This is the story of Edmond Dantès and how, through being teachable, persistent, diligent, and patient, he was able to turn disaster to triumph. Of course the story is fictional, but the truths it teaches are not. They have the power to change your life as much as they did Edmond Dantès.

At the age of 19, Edmond seems to have the perfect life. He is about to become the captain of a ship. He is engaged to a beautiful and kind young woman, and he is well liked by almost everyone who knows him. The key word there is almost. Not everyone likes him. His success stirs up dangerous jealousy among some of his so-called friends.

Danglars, the purser of Dantès' ship, envies his early career success. Fernand Mondego is in love with Dantès' fiancé, and so covets her. His neighbor, the innkeeper, is deeply envious that Dantès has been able to succeed at such an early and young age. Together these three men draft a letter accusing Dantès of treason against the government.

On the very day of his wedding, Dantès is arrested for his alleged crimes. He is convicted of treason, and based on this false testimony, he is sentenced to a life in prison. He is sent to the infamous Château d'If, this dungeon on an island where the most dangerous political prisoners are kept.

While in prison, Dantès meets an old priest who was very, very educated and wise. He had been jailed for his political views, and he was there for the rest of his life. At first, Dantès wanted nothing to do with this old priest or anyone. He was bitter and depressed. He had no hope and he just wanted to die.

Eventually, the old priest helped Dantès to see that he should use his time wisely because a person never knows what the future might bring. Eventually, these two men became friends, and over their 20 years in prison together, the old priest was able to teach Dantès history, science, philosophy, and languages, and many other things, turning him into a very well educated man.

The old priest also bequeathed to Dantès a large treasure hidden on the island of Monte Cristo, and he tells him how to find it should he ever escape. Eventually, the old priest dies and Dantès does find a way to escape, and he then travels to the island of Monte Cristo, and there he finds the enormous treasure.

He considers this fortune a gift from God, given to him for the sole purpose of rewarding those who have tried to help him and stood by him and punishing those who hurt him. Disguising himself, he travels back to Marseille and discovers the three men who betrayed him. He uses his treasure and wisdom, both obtained by his diligence, persistence, and patience, to help those who were true to him and to punish those who betrayed him.

Hopefully, I haven't revealed too much that you won't want to read the book yourself, or at least watch the movie. You'll be inspired by the daily disciplines that Edmond Dantès was willing to impose upon himself to prepare himself for a future that he didn't know would ever come or not. But because he was prepared when it came, it mattered.

This principle of using each day wisely to grow in wisdom and learning and strength is also taught in this old fable. From the very first day of his imprisonment, the wise counselor practiced running up the steps of his cell to the prison door, carrying in each hand the piglet. As the days turned into weeks and the weeks turned into months, the piglets steadily grew into sturdy boars. And with every day of practice, the wise counselor increased his power and strength and agility.

Well, my dear sisters and elders, your inheritance from the Lord is the time He gives you each day. During your mission, you have a schedule that sets forth a huge amount of time for study and learning. During the lockdown, we have all innovated many ways for each of us to learn new skills and refine ourselves even more.

These days of your mission could prove to be like those days in the dungeon for the wise counselor or Edmond Dantès, or they could just be wasted on silly and frivolous actions that will bring you no lasting benefit. As always, you choose.

I love you all and I hope that you will choose to keep growing and building on your useful skills no matter what the future might hold and no matter that you don't know what the future will be. If you do, one day you will be able to look back and say,
So finish the day strong and you know what to say tomorrow morning when you first stand up from your bed. Yep, today is going to be a great day. Talk to you tomorrow.
